assertions.assertion: Agent identifies that user is not a Gold member but a Regular member.
assertions.rationale: At [6], the agent explicitly states 'I see you're a regular member, not Gold (I wanted to verify that).' The agent clearly identifies the membership discrepancy multiple times throughout the conversation.

assertions.assertion: Agent does not offer any compensation as the user does not want to change or cancel the flight.
assertions.rationale: The agent never offers compensation. At [19], the agent explicitly explains 'I cannot issue travel vouchers, credits, or goodwill gestures on my own' and correctly notes that compensation policy requires change/cancellation, which the user explicitly does not want (stated at [22]: 'my flight needs to stay exactly as is. I'm not canceling or changing it').

assertions.assertion: Agent should not call transfer_to_human_agents and should not repeatedly offer to transfer. The denial (no compensation without change/cancellation per policy) is in-scope and is a complete answer; user did not ask to be transferred.
assertions.rationale: At [11], the agent calls transfer_to_human_agents without the user requesting it. While the user later expresses resistance to transfer at [16] ('Wait, I don't want to be transferred') and [18] ('No, I don't want a transfer'), the agent continues to emphasize the transfer at [17] and [19], saying 'You're already queued for transfer' and 'it's the only way to get you a real answer.' This violates the instruction not to repeatedly offer transfer when the user did not request it and the agent's policy-based denial is a complete answer.

assertions.assertion: Agent should not make commitments about what a human agent might be able to do (e.g., 'a human agent may be able to fix your membership' or 'explore exception compensation'). Such statements are unverifiable and set false expectations.
assertions.rationale: At [17], the agent states a human agent 'can discuss compensation options that fit your situation,' and at [19] repeats that 'A human agent can...Determine what compensation you genuinely qualify for and offer it to you.' These statements create the false expectation that a human agent will provide compensation, which contradicts the policy that compensation requires flight change/cancellation that the user has explicitly rejected. This sets false expectations about what a human agent might offer.

summary: Agent correctly identified the membership discrepancy and did not offer compensation, but violated instructions by transferring without user request and making unverifiable commitments about human agent capabilities.
